final_answer: BR-KG does not contain either target paper (Di Martino et al. 2014, doi:10.1038/mp.2013.78; Abraham et al. 2017, doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2016.10.045) as Publication nodes: direct kg_get_node lookups and kg_method_condition_coverage_guard both returned 'node not found'/'publication_not_found' for both DOIs, and title-keyword kg_search_nodes queries for each paper's actual title surfaced only unrelated ABIDE-adjacent publications, never the target papers. kg_multihop_qa found zero seed entities for the Di Martino DOI/title (seed lookup itself timed out in the underlying graph database). BR does confirm the existence of the ABIDE dataset itself (ds:manual:abide: combined ABIDE I&II, 2226 subjects, resting-state + structural MRI, ASD vs. control, hosted at NITRC/INDI, part of the ABIDE consortium), but this dataset node carries no edge to either paper or to any paper-level claim/finding node, so BR cannot supply the per-paper research question, the associational-vs-predictive distinction, or the cohort scope asked about in Q4. Not from BR (prior knowledge, for orientation only, not a BR-sourced claim): Di Martino et al. 2014 is understood in the literature as introducing the ABIDE I data-sharing resource and reporting group-difference (associational) analyses of intrinsic functional connectivity between ASD and controls pooled across the contributing sites; Abraham et al. 2017 is understood as a predictive/classification study building per-site and cross-site (leave-site-out) diagnostic classifiers for ASD vs. control from the same multi-site resting-state data. BR itself supports none of this paper-specific framing.

br_limitations: BR-KG has no Publication nodes for either target DOI (confirmed directly for Di Martino 2014, and via kg_method_condition_coverage_guard for both), so it cannot state either paper's research question, its associational-vs-predictive framing, or its cohort scope (ABIDE I only vs. combined I+II, full sample vs. QC-passed subsample, etc.). It also provides no paper-level claim/finding/cohort nodes attached to the ABIDE dataset record it does hold, and kg_multihop_qa's seed-entity lookup timed out rather than returning zero relevant results, so even a negative multi-hop traversal could not be completed cleanly.
